1920s movement exploring the unconscious; manifesto by Breton, 1924.
French writer (1896-1966), author of Surrealist Manifesto.
Rubbing technique — Max Ernst transferred surface textures to paper.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Bauhaus opened in Weimar in 1919 under Walter Gropius, moved to Dessau in 1925, and was closed by the Nazis in 1933. Its principle — unity of art, craft and industry — shaped 20th-century design.
André Breton's Surrealist Manifesto (1924) called for 'pure psychic automatism' — art driven by the unconscious. Dalí, Magritte, Ernst, Miró and Tanguy followed Breton's lead.
Surrealism developed automatism (drawing without conscious control), frottage (Ernst's rubbings of textured surfaces) and decalcomania as means of bypassing rational composition.
